cameras.label: Upstairs Hallway
cameras._comment: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your real camera IP and credentials. config.json is gitignored and must never be committed.

server._comment: The viewer has NO authentication. Bind localhost and reach it over the tailnet with "tailscale serve --bg 8090". Setting host to 0.0.0.0 exposes a live video feed of the home to every device on the LAN, guests and IoT included.

status._comment: Device status blocks shown above the camera feed. Home Assistant is queried SERVER-SIDE using HA_TOKEN or ~/.ha_token; the token never reaches the browser. Each tile: label, entity, optional states map, alert_when (raw states to highlight), or suffix/alert_below for numbers.

tiles.label: Lock Jam
tiles._comment: Worth its own tile. A jammed deadbolt reports lock state as "unknown", which reads like a glitch rather than a fault: on 2026-09-01 a BE469ZP jammed at 23:50 and sat that way for 13 hours with the dashboard showing a grey "unknown" box. Usually strike-plate misalignment.

climate._comment: Thermostat card above the camera feed. HA is queried SERVER-SIDE; the token never reaches the browser, and the endpoint is read-only. ha_url is optional and defaults to the status block's. Thresholds are in whatever unit HA reports (Settings > System > General) -- no conversion is done. The primary room sensor is the headline number ON PURPOSE: an ecobee can average any sensor participating in the active comfort setting, so the climate entity may read comfortable while a bedroom is cold, and it rounds to a whole degree where the sensor does not. stale_after_seconds guards a known HomeKit failure where a reading freezes at its last value while the entity still looks healthy. Occupancy is deliberately not read; bedroom presence is a separate family decision. Any source may override stale_after_seconds (null disables it for that source): HA only bumps last_updated when a value changes, and a climate entity's values (a whole degree, a humidity point, the HVAC state) legitimately sit still for hours, and even a room sensor only reports on change (an ecobee SmartSensor was seen silent for 32 minutes), so the thermostat gets a much longer window and the room window is an hour.

recording._comment: Clips older than retention_days are deleted by an hourly sweep. Capture is otherwise unbounded (~2.5GB/day observed). 0 disables pruning. Age comes from the filename timestamp, mtime as fallback.

zones._comment: Only the two doorways are detected -- both are close-range and reliable. Anything else resolves by elimination to exit_zone. Polygons are normalized 0-1 coords measured from walk-throughs; re-verify with: python zone_check.py --detect
